item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00153","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C02","C07","C04"],"selected_candidate_label":"C02","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C02 is expressly identified by the child as the prior disapproval involving similar relief, and it supplies both the factual/legal framework and distinctive language of the later memorandum. Both concern fishing-party transportation taxes, the same March 31, 1953 judicial decision, claimants who failed to seek refunds within the limitations period, the continuing purposes of limitations after a changed legal interpretation, discrimination against similarly situated taxpayers, and an undesirable precedent. The child substantially condenses and adapts C02 to eleven new claimants. C07 and C04 share limitations-policy language and the same concluding objections, but neither matches the child's underlying tax, transportation, fishing-party, and judicial-decision facts as C02 does.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The relief sought in this bill is similar to that sought in a bill which I disapproved last year, H.R. 3193, \"For the relief of Toley's Charter Boats, Incorporated, Toley Engebretsen, and Harvey Homlar\".","parent_excerpt":"I AM WITHHOLDING my approval from H. R. 3193, entitled, \"For the relief of Toley's Charter Boats, Incorporated, Toley Engebretsen, and Harvey Homlar.\"","explanation":"The child explicitly identifies C02 as the earlier, substantively similar disapproval."},{"child_excerpt":"On March 31, 1953, a Federal court held that the transportation tax did not apply to the type of transportation involved here.","parent_excerpt":"On March 31, 1953, the District Court for the Northern District of Florida held that the transportation tax was not applicable to amounts paid for fishing parties in situations similar to the one involved in this bill.","explanation":"The child reuses C02's same judicial event and tax treatment, shortening the court description."},{"child_excerpt":"The basic purposes underlying the statute of limitations continue to obtain in cases where a taxpayer, after having paid a tax, discovers that the interpretation of the law has been changed by a judicial decision.","parent_excerpt":"The basic purposes underlying the statute of limitations continue in force even in cases where a taxpayer, after having paid a tax, discovers that the interpretation of the law has been changed by a judicial decision or by a modification in regulations and rulings.","explanation":"This is distinctive, near-verbatim policy language, with only minor compression and substitution."},{"child_excerpt":"Granting relief in this case would discriminate against other taxpayers similarly situated and would create an undesirable precedent.","parent_excerpt":"The bill, therefore, would unfairly discriminate against other taxpayers similarly situated and would create an undesirable precedent.","explanation":"The child closely reproduces C02's ultimate objection and conclusion."}]}
